Headline: First U.S. excavator patent (Otis steam shovel)
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1839... the first U.S. patent for a steam-powered excavator was granted to William Otis of Philadelphia for a 'crane excavator for excavating and removing earth.' Every hydraulic excavator on a job site today is a descendant of that machine. From hand shovels to hydraulic excavators, it's all about moving material efficiently — which is exactly what we do with every load of RCC. 🚜

Headline: Caterpillar Inc. founded
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1925... Holt Manufacturing Co. and C.L. Best Tractor Co. merged to form Caterpillar Inc., uniting two rival tractor makers into the company that would go on to define earthmoving for the next century. Cat dozers and loaders move a lot of RCC across our yards every week. 🟡

Headline: Caterpillar joins the Dow Jones Industrial Average
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1991... Caterpillar joined the Dow Jones Industrial Average, replacing Navistar International. A reminder that heavy equipment isn't just iron and dirt — it's a cornerstone of the American economy.
Photo Suggestion: Stock photo of Cat equipment lineup

Headline: Komatsu founded
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1921... Komatsu Ltd. was founded in Komatsu City, Japan, starting out as a maker of cast-iron tools and mining equipment. Over 100 years later, it's one of the biggest names in excavators and dozers worldwide.
Photo Suggestion: Stock photo of a Komatsu excavator/dozer

Headline: Jaw crusher patented (Eli Whitney Blake)
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1858... Eli Whitney Blake of New Haven, CT was granted U.S. Patent No. 20,542 for his 'machine for crushing stone' — the first practical jaw crusher. The toggle-jaw design he patented is still the basic blueprint for jaw crushers used today, including the ones that turn demolition concrete into the RCC we deliver across PA, NJ, and DE. 🪨

Headline: Manitowoc Company founded
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1902... the Manitowoc Company was founded in Manitowoc, Wisconsin as a shipbuilding operation. It later became one of the world's leading crane manufacturers — the same type of cranes used on demolition and concrete recycling sites today.
Photo Suggestion: Stock photo of a crawler crane on a demo site

Headline: Euclid Road Machinery incorporated
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1931... Euclid Road Machinery Co. was incorporated in Ohio, helping pioneer the off-highway dump truck. Without haul trucks like these, modern crushing and aggregate operations couldn't move material at scale. 🚛
Photo Suggestion: Yard photo of a dump truck being loaded with RCC

Headline: Kobe Steel founded
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1905... Kobe Steel Ltd. was founded in Japan. Decades later, its construction machinery division would spin off and become Kobelco, now a major excavator manufacturer worldwide.
Photo Suggestion: Stock photo of a Kobelco excavator

Headline: Roots of Mack Trucks formed
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1911... Saurer Motor Truck Co. merged with Mack Brothers Motor Car Co. to form the International Motor Truck Company — the roots of Mack Trucks, headquartered just up the road in Allentown, PA. Our RCC moves on trucks built tough like these every single day. 🚚
Photo Suggestion: Photo of a tri-axle dump truck loaded with RCC

Headline: World's largest dump truck unveiled (BelAZ 75710)
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 2013... BelAZ unveiled the 75710 in Belarus — the largest dump truck ever built, with a payload capacity of about 450 tons. Our trucks aren't quite that big, but the job is the same: move heavy material, efficiently. 😄

Headline: Hitachi Construction Machinery established
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1970... Hitachi Construction Machinery Co., Ltd. was formally established in Japan, growing into one of the largest excavator manufacturers in the world.
Photo Suggestion: Stock photo of a Hitachi excavator

Headline: JCB founded
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1945... Joseph Cyril Bamford founded JCB in a 12x15-foot rented garage in Uttoxeter, England — the same day his son Anthony was born. Eight years later, JCB invented the modern backhoe loader, the machine that could dig AND load, changing construction forever. 🟡

Headline: America Recycles Day
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 Today is America Recycles Day, a national observance recognized by the EPA every November 15. Every ton of Recycled Crushed Concrete (RCC) we process is concrete that didn't end up in a landfill — recycling on a massive scale, every single day. ♻️

Headline: Origin of the 'Caterpillar' name
Ready-to-Post Caption: 📅 On this day in 1904 (Thanksgiving Day)... Benjamin Holt demonstrated the first successful track-type tractor in a peat field near Stockton, CA. Watching it crawl along on its tracks, a photographer remarked it moved 'just like a caterpillar' — and the name stuck, eventually becoming the most famous brand in construction equipment. 🐛➡️🚜
